title: Notre voyage en français
oneGoal: Students reflect on their French learning journey throughout the year
decisionPoints: How much French growth can students recognize in themselves?
Do they need visual supports to remember earlier learning?
Should we use photos or work samples to trigger memories?
progression: Begins the year review by activating memories of their French learning journey
realWorldConnection: People look back on their year to see how much they've grown and learned

title: Nos premiers mots français
oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate the first French words they learned
decisionPoints: Which early French words do students still remember?
Do they need prompting with pictures or gestures?
Should we recreate some early learning activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing specifically on early vocabulary acquisition
realWorldConnection: We remember our 'firsts' - first words, first steps, first day of school

title: Chansons et comptines préférées
oneGoal: Students revisit and perform favorite French songs and rhymes from the year
decisionPoints: Which songs do students remember most clearly?
Do they need lyric supports or can they sing from memory?
Should we add new movements to familiar songs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by celebrating musical and rhythmic language learning
realWorldConnection: Music helps us remember and connects us to happy memories

title: Histoires que nous aimons
oneGoal: Students revisit favorite French stories and books from throughout the year
decisionPoints: Which stories had the biggest impact on students?
Do they remember story details or just general impressions?
Should we reread stories or just look at pictures and discuss?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by celebrating narrative and reading experiences
realWorldConnection: Favorite stories stay with us and shape how we see the world

title: Nos réussites en français
oneGoal: Students identify and celebrate specific French learning achievements
decisionPoints: Can students articulate what they're proud of learning?
Do they need examples to recognize their own growth?
Should achievements be academic or social/emotional?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by moving from content review to metacognitive reflection
realWorldConnection: Recognizing our achievements helps build confidence and motivation

title: Défis surmontés ensemble
oneGoal: Students reflect on challenges they overcame in French learning
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable discussing things that were difficult?
Should challenges be framed positively as growth opportunities?
Do they need support to see how they overcame difficulties?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by acknowledging growth through overcoming difficulties
realWorldConnection: Everyone faces challenges, and overcoming them makes us stronger

title: Amis et moments spéciaux
oneGoal: Students reflect on friendships and special moments in French class
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students sharing positive peer relationships?
Should focus be on group memories or individual friendships?
Do they need prompting to remember collaborative learning moments?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by celebrating social and emotional aspects of learning
realWorldConnection: Learning is more meaningful when we share it with friends

title: Créations dont nous sommes fiers
oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate creative work produced throughout the year
decisionPoints: Which student creations show the most growth or effort?
Should we display work or have students present it?
Do they remember the process of creating or just the final products?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by focusing on tangible evidence of learning and creativity
realWorldConnection: Artists and creators look back at their work to see their journey

title: Commencer notre portfolio
oneGoal: Students begin organizing their year's work into a meaningful portfolio
decisionPoints: How much independence can students handle in portfolio organization?
Should portfolios be chronological or thematic?
Do they need templates or can they create their own structure?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by transitioning from reflection to documentation and organization
realWorldConnection: People create portfolios to show their best work and growth over time

title: Choisir nos meilleurs exemples
oneGoal: Students select their best work samples for portfolio inclusion
decisionPoints: What criteria should students use to select 'best' work?
Do they need guidance on variety vs. quality?
Should selection focus on growth evidence or final products?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by developing critical thinking and self-evaluation skills
realWorldConnection: We choose our best examples when applying for jobs or showing our abilities

title: Raconter notre histoire d'apprentissage
oneGoal: Students create narratives explaining their learning journey and growth
decisionPoints: Can students articulate their learning story in French?
Do they need sentence starters or story templates?
Should stories be written, oral, or illustrated?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by adding reflective narrative to portfolio selections
realWorldConnection: Everyone has a learning story - how we grew and changed over time

title: Partager avec nos familles
oneGoal: Students prepare to share their portfolios and growth with families
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students presenting their learning to families?
Do they need practice or scripts for family presentations?
Should sharing be formal presentations or informal conversations?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by preparing to communicate learning beyond the classroom
realWorldConnection: We share our achievements and growth with people who care about us

title: Célébrer nos progrès
oneGoal: Students participate in a celebration of their French learning progress
decisionPoints: What type of celebration would be most meaningful for students?
Should celebration be individual recognition or group achievement?
Do families need to be included in the celebration?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by formally recognizing and honoring learning achievements
realWorldConnection: Celebrations mark important milestones and achievements in our lives

title: Regarder vers l'avenir
oneGoal: Students set goals and express hopes for continued French learning
decisionPoints: Are students excited about continuing French or feeling anxious?
Should goals be specific skills or general enthusiasm?
Do they understand French will continue in their education?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by connecting current achievement to future learning possibilities
realWorldConnection: Setting goals helps us continue growing and reaching for new achievements

title: Jeux de révision amusants
oneGoal: Students play engaging games reviewing vocabulary and concepts from the year
decisionPoints: Which review games engage students most effectively?
Should games focus on vocabulary, grammar, or communication?
Do students prefer competitive or collaborative game formats?
progression: Extends Lesson 14 by reinforcing learning through enjoyable review activities
realWorldConnection: Playing games with what we've learned makes knowledge stick and brings joy

title: Spectacle de talents français
oneGoal: Students showcase their French abilities through performances or presentations
decisionPoints: What performance formats appeal to different student personalities?
Should performances be individual or group-based?
Do students need time to prepare or prefer spontaneous sharing?
progression: Extends Lesson 15 by providing authentic opportunities to demonstrate French proficiency
realWorldConnection: Talent shows let us share our abilities and celebrate what makes each person special

title: Lettres à nous-mêmes
oneGoal: Students write letters to their future selves about their French learning experience
decisionPoints: Can students write simple letters in French or need English support?
Should letters focus on advice, memories, or encouragement?
Do they understand the concept of 'future self'?
progression: Extends Lesson 16 by encouraging deeper reflection and connection to future learning
realWorldConnection: Writing to our future selves helps us remember important moments and lessons

title: Cadeau pour la prochaine classe
oneGoal: Students create something helpful for next year's Grade 1 French students
decisionPoints: What would be most helpful for incoming Grade 1 students?
Should gifts be advice, encouragement, or practical resources?
Do students remember what would have helped them at the beginning?
progression: Extends Lesson 17 by channeling reflection into service and mentorship
realWorldConnection: Helping others who are starting their journey is a way to give back and show growth

title: Temps libre français
oneGoal: Students engage in free choice French activities based on their interests
decisionPoints: What French activities do students choose when given freedom?
Should choices be from provided options or completely open?
Do students need guidance to make meaningful choices?
progression: Extends Lesson 18 by honoring student voice and choice in their learning
realWorldConnection: Having choices about what we do helps us feel ownership and enjoyment

title: Au revoir et à bientôt!
oneGoal: Students celebrate the end of Grade 1 French and look forward to continuing
decisionPoints: How can we make the ending feel celebratory rather than sad?
Should focus be on endings or new beginnings?
Do students need reassurance about continuing French learning?
progression: Extends Lesson 19 by providing closure while maintaining excitement for continued French learning
realWorldConnection: Saying goodbye to one chapter means we're ready to start the next adventure
